headline: FIFA confirms Bangladesh to play in ASEAN Cup as India withdraws
summary: The national team will compete in Jakarta from September 24 to October 4, replacing India due to scheduling conflicts.
details: FIFA has officially confirmed Bangladesh's participation in the FIFA ASEAN Cup, which will take place in Jakarta, Indonesia, from September 24 to October 4.

The Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) confirmed the news following an executive committee meeting on Saturday, stating they had received a positive response from FIFA after applying for the tournament.
Bangladesh enters the competition as a last-minute replacement for India, who withdrew from the tournament due to clashes with other international assignments.
The national team has been placed in Group A, where they will face hosts Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore.
Group B of the tournament will feature Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Pakistan.
The BFF executive committee has announced that a national team camp will be called shortly, following discussions with head coach Thomas Dooley.

Bangladesh is heading to Jakarta! 🇧🇩

FIFA has confirmed the national team's spot in the ASEAN Cup.

FIFA has officially confirmed Bangladesh's participation in the FIFA ASEAN Cup, which will take place in Jakarta, Indonesia, from September 24 to October 4.

The Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) confirmed the news following an executive committee meeting on Saturday, stating they had received a positive response from FIFA after applying for the tournament.

Bangladesh enters the competition as a last-minute replacement for India, who withdrew from the tournament due to clashes with other international assignments.

The national team has been placed in Group A, where they will face hosts Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore.

Group B of the tournament will feature Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, and Pakistan.

The BFF executive committee has announced that a national team camp will be called shortly, following discussions with head coach Thomas Dooley.

headline_marked: Cabinet reshuffle: [[Zahir Uddin Swapon appointed PM’s political adviser]]
headline: Cabinet reshuffle: Zahir Uddin Swapon appointed PM’s political adviser
summary: The former Information and Broadcasting Minister has been assigned the role with the rank and privileges of a minister.
details: Zahir Uddin Swapon has been appointed as the political adviser to the prime minister, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division on Friday.
Prior to this appointment, Swapon resigned from his position as the Minister for Information and Broadcasting.
His resignation was formally accepted by President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, as confirmed by a separate gazette notification.
In a simultaneous reshuffle, Andaleeve Rahman Partho, chairman of the Bangladesh Jatiya Party, was sworn in as a minister and given charge of the Information and Broadcasting Ministry.
The appointment of Swapon as political adviser was made under Rules 3B(i) and 3B(ii) of the Rules of Business, 1996.
In his new role, Swapon will be entitled to the rank, salary, allowances, and other benefits associated with a minister's position.
The notification was signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani by order of the president.
caption:
From Minister to Political Adviser: Zahir Uddin Swapon takes on a new role in the government.

Zahir Uddin Swapon has been appointed as the political adviser to the prime minister, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division on Friday.

Prior to this appointment, Swapon resigned from his position as the Minister for Information and Broadcasting.

His resignation was formally accepted by President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, as confirmed by a separate gazette notification.

In a simultaneous reshuffle, Andaleeve Rahman Partho, chairman of the Bangladesh Jatiya Party, was sworn in as a minister and given charge of the Information and Broadcasting Ministry.

The appointment of Swapon as political adviser was made under Rules 3B(i) and 3B(ii) of the Rules of Business, 1996.

In his new role, Swapon will be entitled to the rank, salary, allowances, and other benefits associated with a minister's position.

The notification was signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani by order of the president.
